channel.title: Disability Scoop – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Disability Scoop – Bias and Credibility (disabilityscoop.com)

item.title: When Slowing Down Can Save A Life: Training Law Enforcement To Understand Autism
item.description: In a room filled with pounding noises and clanging cowbells, sheriff's deputies learn that sometimes the best way to handle a crisis is to simply wait.

item.title: DC Schools Discriminated Against Students With Disabilities, OCR Finds
item.description: The school district, which has one of highest rates of special education complaints in the nation, often forces families to sue for their kids to receive services, the U.S. Department of Education said.

item.title: With Settlement, Lyft Pushed To Improve Accessibility
item.description: A major ride-sharing service is facing new pressure to ensure equal access for people with disabilities.

item.title: How A Trump-Backed Voting Bill Could Impact People With Disabilities
item.description: President Donald Trump says voting changes are his number one priority, but concerns are running high that his plan could make it harder for people with disabilities to cast their ballots.

item.title: More College Students Are Seeking Disability Accommodations. Why?
item.description: The number of college students who register as having a disability has increased across the country. Nowhere has that trend been more pronounced — or debated — than at Stanford University.

item.title: Social Security Eyes SSI Reforms
item.description: The Social Security Administration says a new team is working to improve the efficiency of its Supplemental Security Income program and help recipients comply with requirements.

item.title: Adidas Introduces Shoe Geared Towards Athletes With Down Syndrome
item.description: After a multiyear collaboration with individuals with Down syndrome and other disabilities, one of the world's largest footwear companies is rolling out a shoe designed to specifically meet their needs.

item.title: The Fight To Stay Home: How A Lawsuit Could Upend Disability Care
item.description: Advocates say if Texas and eight other states win a lawsuit arguing that Section 504 is unconstitutional, it could mean that Medicaid waivers paying for community living are no longer required.

item.title: Ed Department May Offload Special Education Soon, Advocates Warn
item.description: As the U.S. Department of Education continues to transfer responsibilities to other agencies, disability advocates are concerned that special education could be up next.

item.title: This Entrepreneur With Down Syndrome Is Building A Booming Spice Blend Brand
item.description: Max Crawford is 22 and has Down syndrome and products from his budding seasoning business are sold in 150 stores across the Midwest.

item.title: Autism Dating Show Returning To Netflix
item.description: An Emmy-winning documentary series chronicling the lives of adults with autism who are looking for love is returning.

item.title: Nation's Disability Services System Faces 'Unprecedented' Threats
item.description: Already facing nearly $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts, disability advocates are now worried that new efforts to crack down on fraud and trim state budgets will erode access to community-based services.

item.title: Apprentice Program Offers 'Student Teaching On Steroids' To Help Fill Special Ed Shortages
item.description: School districts need high-qualified special education instructors. A teacher apprenticeship program hopes to help fill the gap and prevent turnover.

item.title: To Master Life Skills, Young People With Autism And Down Syndrome Turn To Virtual Reality
item.description: In a controlled, low-risk environment, participants in a pilot program build confidence and master everyday tasks like crossing the street, riding a bus or making a purchase, all at their own pace.

item.title: SeaWorld, Other Theme Parks Accused Of Violating ADA
item.description: The U.S. Department of Justice is accusing several major theme parks of failing to accommodate people with disabilities in violation of the Americans with Disabilities Act.
